sanskrit_verse: ubhayoḥ pratibhūr grāhyaḥ samarthaḥ kāryanirṇaye // BrhS_1,1.156
sph_interpretive_translation: In the resolution of a matter, the surety or representative who stands equally responsible for both parties shall be accepted as competent to act.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority arises from capacity to ensure completion of dharma-karya
Causation lies in the conscious assumption of mutual responsibility
Capacity-based responsibility extends beyond individual agency to include representational integrity
Restoration logic requires that all stakeholders have access to a neutral yet empowered arbiter
Consciousness alignment occurs when representation upholds samartha-dharma without partiality
executable_legal_axioms: IF any dispute involves two or more parties AND a neutral representative exists who has assumed mutual liability THEN that representative MUST be granted procedural authority
IF a party invokes completion-process AND no direct resolution is possible THEN a samartha-pratibhu MUST be identified and empowered
IF a pratibhu accepts liability for both sides THEN their decision-making capacity SHALL NOT be questioned on grounds of personal interest
IF a case reaches final review without settlement THEN the presence of a pratibhu SHALL determine admissibility for judicial processing
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme Court level, this verse establishes the principle that where dual-party obligations exist unresolved, the presence of a mutually acknowledged representative confers jurisdictional validity upon the matter. The Court must recognize such representatives as lawful conduits for final settlement, bypassing lower procedural constraints.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramana-based causality identifies the pratibhu as the stabilizing axis around which karmic entanglement resolves. Their role aligns action with dharma rather than blame. Anupurvasah shows how misalignment precedes dispute; thus restoration flows through the pratibhu's reassertion of shared duty. There is no punitive element—only realignment via conscious representation.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate pratibhu acknowledgment protocol wherein both disputants confirm acceptance of third-party representation
Deploy capacity-assumption ceremony led by Nyaya-bindu wherein pratibhu affirms readiness to restore balance
Execute samartha-dharma alignment process ensuring no punitive residue remains in either party’s consciousness
Finalize kriya-nishpatti through pratibhu-mediated agreement witnessed by at least three conscious observers
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this directive is established. The pratibhu embodies samartha-dharma. Justice flows not through judgment but through integration. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness alone adjudicates.
